correctness.rationale: For commuting unitaries, joint unitary diagonalization reduces the terminal operator norm to |Σ_{j=0}^k binom(N,j)(z−1)^j| at each unit-circle relative eigenvalue z. Exact free-N Chebyshev algebra yields four signed factorization identities in u=1−Re(z). Positivity of each N-prefactor and Δ²=2max(u) gives necessary and sufficient phase frontiers and realization in dimension one. The symbolic program verifies each free-N polynomial equality; 1020 checks also cover independent recurrence and commuting-matrix cases. No finite sample is used to infer the all-N statement.

value.rationale: Phase mismatch is a recognized barrier in nondiffusive time-parallel integration. The exact k=1/2 obstruction, k=3 first nontrivial energy-safe regime and k=4 enlarged regime distinguish correction counts by a sharp, realizable spectral design tolerance that scales like N^{-1} in phase. The five-window counterexample exhibits initial expansive sweeps followed by true terminal-block contraction, separating operational one-block stability from a priori iteration-error bounds. This supplies a physically motivated sharp stability design criterion, not an arbitrary polynomial table.
